chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Studying vibes and tympani but having to earn a living
summary: He studied vibes and a little tympani but left school to make a living, wishing he had studied more.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Plays his ass off. You mentioned in your advice to young musicians, that they should -- if they're going to play reed instruments, they should learn to play all of the wind instruments and so forth. Did you follow your own advice and learn other percussion instruments?

Yeah, well, I learned, but I could only learn to a certain extent. I -- that was one of the things that I really hated. I studied vibes at the time, and then I studied a little tympani. But I had to get out and make a living, because my sister raised me, like I told you before. She was like my mother, and so when I went on the road, well, that just blew all the rest of my schooling and everything. So then the rest of it, you just had to be natural ability with -- and then I'd have to lean on what I had learned,
which I would have loved to have gone through and played vibes like you. You knocked me out when I heard you. Yeah, but, I mean, I just wished I could have studied more.
Did you ever run into some shows where you had to double tympany or --
Yeah, right, this is what I mean, seeing to certain parts and things like that. And I could do just enough of it to get the effect that was needed.

Right, and so -- but I would have liked to have been a virtuoso or whatever you want to call it on these instruments. Yeah. But after you get caught up in the business of making a living, and then playing and trying to get your -- raising a family and all of that, something has to give, and so your studying has to give, you give it up.
